page: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 128 dedicated vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores running at 3.9 GHz on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities across multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Its DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth for both small and large blocks. Advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, support high-throughput operations, as evidenced by top-tier performance in Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests.

The instance is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, database operations, and static web serving, all of which scored in the top tier. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models. However, single-core performance represents a relative tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core metrics falling into the average category. This makes the instance highly cost-efficient for parallelized, multi-threaded workloads rather than single-threaded tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs and 64 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It is configured with 256.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and strong cryptographic execution, aided by AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. While single-core performance is average, its multi-threaded capabilities excel in software compilation, database operations, and large-scale LLM prompt processing. This profile offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized enterprise workloads.
